statement.name: Ramsey's theorem on general domains
statement.definition: Instances are pairs ⟨X, c⟩ with X an infinite set and c : [X]^n → k; solutions are infinite homogeneous subsets of X.
statement.facts: RT^n_k ≡W General-RT^n_k for all n, k ≥ 1 (Proposition 8.3.4(1)), and RCA0 proves ∀n∀k [RT^n_k ↔ General-RT^n_k].

statement.name: A problem with finite errors
statement.definition: For a problem P whose solutions are subsets of ω, P^fe has the same instances as P and its solutions are all sets Z =* Y for some P-solution Y.
statement.facts: COH is Weihrauch equivalent to the parallelization of (RT^1_2)^fe (Corollary 8.4.15). The same instances of the two problems, and uniformly computable-in-the-jump characterizations of their solutions, are given in Theorem 8.4.13 (Jockusch–Stephan).

statement.name: Tree antichain theorem (Conidis)
statement.definition: Any infinite c.e. subtree of 2^{<N} which is completely branching contains an infinite antichain. This is not the catalogue tac, which is the paper's 'CAC for trees'.
statement.facts: TAC + BΣ⁰₂ is equivalent to CAC for trees over RCA0 and over computable reduction (Theorem 2.5). TAC is equivalent to SAC (Lemma 2.12). TAC does not imply BΣ⁰₂ or CAC for trees (Corollary 3.8). TAC implies HYP (Corollary 5.7). TAC has a computable instance with no P-computable solution for any low P (Corollary 5.3), and a computable instance all of whose solutions are of hyperimmune degree (Theorem 5.6, Conidis). For any uniform sequence of infinite Δ⁰₂ sets there is a computable instance of TAC that none of them solves (Theorem 5.1). TAC is implied by CAC (Conidis).

statement.name: Set antichain theorem
statement.definition: Every infinite completely branching set X ⊆ 2^{<N} has an infinite antichain.
statement.facts: SAC is equivalent to TAC over RCA0 (Lemma 2.12). Computable instances of SAC are solved by a measure-one set of oracles (Proposition 3.3). 2-RAN implies SAC over RCA0 (Proposition 3.7). Every set of degree DNC_h(∅′) with h computable computes a solution of an instance of SAC (Proposition 3.11).

statement.notation: CAC for c.e. trees / CAC for c.e. binary trees
statement.name: Chain-antichain theorem for c.e. (binary) trees
statement.definition: Every infinite c.e. (binary) subtree of N^{<N} has an infinite path or an infinite antichain.
statement.facts: Both are equivalent to CAC for trees and to TAC + BΣ⁰₂ over RCA0 and over computable reduction (Theorem 2.5). Both imply TAC and ∀k RT¹_k (Propositions 2.6 and 2.7). SHER implies CAC for c.e. trees (Proposition 6.3).

statement.name: Ramsey's theorem for pairs restricted to semi-hereditary colorings
statement.definition: For any 2-coloring f of pairs which is semi-hereditary for some color, there is an infinite f-homogeneous set. Introduced by Dorais et al. [8].
statement.facts: SHER is equivalent to CAC for trees over RCA0 and over computable reduction (Propositions 6.3 and 6.6). ADS implies SHER (via Proposition 4.1 and Proposition 6.6). SHER for stable colorings is equivalent to CAC for stable c.e. trees (Corollary 7.9).

statement.name: Paper's 2-RAN (Definition 3.6)
statement.definition: For every sequence of uniformly Π⁰₂ binary trees T_n with µ([T_n]) > 1 − 2^{-n}, there are n and X with X ∈ [T_n]. This is not the catalogue ran2.
statement.facts: RCA0 ⊢ 2-RAN ⇒ SAC (Proposition 3.7). Slaman (unpublished) proved that 2-RAN does not imply BΣ⁰₂ over RCA0.

statement.name: Infinite set with semi-ancestry for some color
statement.definition: For any 2-coloring of pairs there is an infinite set which has semi-ancestry for some color.
statement.facts: It implies D²₂ and BΣ⁰₂ over RCA0. It implies RT²₂ over RCA0 and over computable reduction. It is equivalent to RT²₂.

statement.name: Infinite set with semi-heredity for some color
statement.definition: For any 2-coloring of pairs there is an infinite set which is semi-hereditary for some color.
statement.facts: It implies ADS over RCA0 and over computable reduction. It implies RT²₂ over RCA0. It is unknown whether RT²₂ is computably reducible to it (Question 8.4).

statement.name: CAC for stable trees
statement.definition: CAC restricted to stable (c.e.) trees, where a tree is stable if every node has either almost all nodes incomparable to it or almost all comparable to it.
statement.facts: SADS implies CAC for stable c.e. trees over RCA0 (Proposition 7.3). CAC for stable c.e. trees admits low solutions (Corollary 7.5). CAC for stable trees implies ∀k RT¹_k, and it is equivalent to CAC for stable c.e. trees and to SHER for stable colorings over RCA0 (Lemma 7.6, Corollary 7.9).

statement.name: Bolzano–Weierstraß theorem on a computable metric space X
statement.definition: BWT_X(x_n) is the set of cluster points of a sequence (x_n) in X with relatively compact range. Only the case X = R is in the catalogue (bwt).
statement.facts: BWT_X ≡sW K_X′ (Theorem 11.2). BWT_X ≡sW BWT_{0,1}^N for rich spaces X, so BWT_{R^n} ≡sW BWT_{l2} ≡sW BWT_[0,1] ≡sW BWT_{0,1}^N ≡sW BWT_{N^N}. BWT_2 ≡sW LLPO′ and BWT_N ≡sW (LLPO*)′. BWT_n <W BWT_{n+1} <W BWT_N <W BWT_R (Theorem 13.4). BWT_N is idempotent. BWT_2 ≰W lim.

statement.name: Cluster point problem and its unique version
statement.definition: CL_X = C_X ∘ L_X: given a sequence in X that has a cluster point, find a cluster point. UCL_X is the restriction to sequences with a unique cluster point.
statement.facts: C_X′ ≡sW CL_X (Theorem 9.4). CL_{N^N} ≡sW C_{N^N} (Theorem 9.16). BWT_R <W CL_R. UCL_R and CL_N are incomparable with BWT_R (Theorem 12.4). CL_R ≤sW L′ (uniform relative low basis theorem). Every computable sequence with a cluster point has a cluster point that is low relative to the halting problem.

statement.name: Unique Bolzano–Weierstraß theorem
statement.definition: The restriction of BWT_X to sequences with a unique cluster point.
statement.facts: UBWT_X = lim_X for Hausdorff X (Proposition 11.21). UBWT_R ≡sW lim and UBWT_N ≡sW C_N (Corollaries 11.22 and 11.24).

statement.name: Monotone convergence theorem (as a Weihrauch problem)
statement.definition: MCT is the partial function (x_n) ↦ sup x_n on bounded monotone sequences of reals.
statement.facts: MCT ≡sW sup ≡sW lim (Fact 11.26). BWT_R ≡sW WKL ∗ MCT (Corollary 11.27).

statement.name: Antithesis of Specker's theorem
statement.definition: Given a sequence of reals eventually bounded away from every point of [0,1], find N and k such that |x_n − x| > 2^{-k} for all x in [0,1] and n ≥ N.
statement.facts: AS ≡W C_N ≡W BCT (Theorem 15.2).

statement.name: Compact choice
statement.definition: K_X chooses a point from a nonempty compact set given with negative compact information (κ−). KC_X is C_X restricted to nonempty compact sets.
statement.facts: K_N ≡sW LLPO*. K_N <W KC_N ≡sW C_N. K_X ≡sW KC_X ≡sW C_X for computably compact X. K_X ≡sW K_{0,1}^N for rich X. K_R ≡sW C_{0,1}^N ≡sW WKL.

statement.notation: f′ (derivative / jump of a Weihrauch degree)
statement.name: Derivative of a multi-valued function
statement.definition: f′ is f with the input representation δ replaced by δ∘lim.
statement.facts: f ≤sW f′. f ≤sW g implies f′ ≤sW g′. g′ ≡sW g ∗s lim, and ≡W g ∗ lim if g is a cylinder. Derivatives are strong fractals. C_{N^N}′ ≡sW C_{N^N}.

statement.name: Large Ramsey Theorem (Ramsey's theorem for exactly ω-large sets, the Schreier barrier)
statement.definition: For every k-coloring of the exactly ω-large finite sets (|s| = 1 + min s), there is an infinite homogeneous set.
statement.facts: Computable instances have ∅^(ω)-computable solutions (cited from Carlucci–Zdanowski and Clote). Some computable 2-coloring has all solutions computing ∅^(ω). RT^{!ω}_2 is equivalent to ACA+_0 over RCA0 (Theorem 3.2). It implies FS^{!ω} over RCA0 (Corollary 3.5). Open: whether RT^{!ω}_2 ≤sW TS^{!ω} or ≤sW FS^{!ω}.

statement.name: Large Free Set Theorem
statement.definition: For every f : [N]^{!ω} → N there is an infinite H such that f(s) ∉ H \ s for all s ∈ [H]^{!ω}.
statement.facts: FS^{!ω} ≤sW RT^{!ω}_2 (Theorem 3.4). TS^{!ω} ≤sW FS^{!ω} (Theorem 3.7). RRT^{!ω}_2 ≤sW FS^{!ω} (Proposition 3.11). There is a computable instance all of whose free sets compute ∅^(ω) (Corollary 4.7). FS^{!ω} implies ACA+_0 over RCA0 (Corollary 4.8).

statement.name: Large Thin Set Theorem
statement.definition: For every f : [N]^{!ω} → N there is an infinite H with f([H]^{!ω}) ≠ N.
statement.facts: There is a computable coloring such that every infinite thin set uniformly computes ∅^(ω) (Theorem 4.6). It implies ACA+_0 over RCA0 (Corollary 4.8). TS^{!ω} ≤sW FS^{!ω} (Theorem 3.7). TS^{!ω} is strongly Weihrauch equivalent to the version omitting infinitely many colors (Proposition 3.8). TS^{!ω} ≤sW RRT^{!(ω+1)}_2 (Proposition 4.11).

statement.name: Large Rainbow Ramsey Theorem
statement.definition: For every k-bounded f : [N]^{!ω} → N there is an infinite H on which f is injective on [H]^{!ω}.
statement.facts: RRT^{!ω}_k ≤sW RT^{!ω}_k, and this is provable in RCA0 (Theorem 3.10). RRT^{!ω}_2 ≤sW FS^{!ω} (Proposition 3.11). It implies RRT^n_k over RCA0, with RRT^n_k ≤sW RRT^{!ω}_k (Proposition 3.12). There is a computable 2-bounded instance with no arithmetical solution (Theorem 4.10). It admits strong cone avoidance (Corollary 6.28), so it does not code ∅′ and does not imply ACA0. Open: whether RRT^{!ω}_k ≤sW FS^{!ω} for all k.

statement.name: Generalized Rainbow Ramsey Theorem for a barrier B
statement.definition: For every k-bounded coloring f : B → N, B ⊆ [N]^{<ω}, there is an infinite f-rainbow.
statement.facts: For computable barriers of order type ω^ω and k = 2, some computable instance has all rainbows computing ∅′ (Proposition 5.10). For computably ω-bounded barriers it admits strong cone avoidance (Corollary 6.28).

statement.name: Progressive Free Set Theorem (b-constrained progressive colorings into finite subsets)
statement.definition: For every b-constrained progressive coloring f : B → [N]^{<ω} there is an infinite f-free set.
statement.facts: For B = [N]^{≤h(·)} with h computable it admits strong cone avoidance (Theorem 6.14), strong PA avoidance and other notions of avoidance (Remark 6.27). For some computable barrier of order type ω^ω it does not admit cone avoidance (Proposition 6.13). With a non-computable bound b it does not admit strong cone avoidance (Proposition 6.26).

statement.name: k-Constrained Free Set Theorem
statement.definition: For every f : B → [N]^{≤k} there is an infinite f-free set.
statement.facts: FS^{≤n}_k admits strong cone avoidance (Proposition 6.8). FS^{≤!ω}_1 has a computable instance all of whose free sets compute ∅^(ω) (Corollary 4.7). Without the constant bound the statement is false (Proposition 6.9).

statement.name: Thin Set Theorem for finite colorings
statement.definition: For every coloring f : [N]^n → k there is an infinite set H thin for f, i.e. f([H]^n) ≠ k.
statement.facts: There is a uniformly computable family of colorings f_{n,k} : [N]^{n+k} → n such that every infinite thin set uniformly computes ∅^(k) (Lemma 4.5). A computable coloring [N]^{n+1} → n has every thin set computing ∅′ (Lemma 4.3).

statement.name: Valuation Extension Lemma
statement.definition: For every frame (W,R) and every assignment v : W × Prop → 2 there is a full Kripke valuation V : W × Fml → 2 on (W,R) extending v.
statement.facts: Provable in ACA+_0 (Theorem 2.5). Equivalent over RCA0 to ACA+_0 (Theorem 2.24). Implies ACA0 over RCA0 (Proposition 2.9). Corollary 2.13 gives a computable frame all of whose valuations compute ∅^(ω). Existence of some valuation on every frame is also equivalent to ACA+_0 (Theorem 2.24).

statement.name: Restricted Valuation Extension Lemma
statement.definition: For every frame, assignment v and k there is a k-restricted valuation (defined on formulas of modal degree ≤ k) extending v.
statement.facts: Equivalent to ACA'_0 over RCA0 (Theorem 2.25). Provable in ACA'_0 (Corollary 2.6). For standard k the k-restricted version is provable in ACA0 (Corollary 2.7). Existence of 1-restricted valuations on all frames is equivalent to ACA0 (Theorem 2.26).

statement.name: Frame definability for Geach axioms
statement.definition: For a frame F, the confluence-type first-order condition on iterated accessibility is equivalent to F validating Ga(i,j,m,n;φ) for all φ.
statement.facts: Equivalent to ACA+_0 over RCA0 (Theorem 2.24). The weak version, restricted to k-restricted valuations, is equivalent to ACA'_0 (Theorem 2.25).

statement.name: Frame definability for GL
statement.definition: F is transitive with no infinite R-ascending sequence iff F validates □(□φ→φ)→□φ for all φ.
statement.facts: Equivalent to ACA+_0 over RCA0 (Theorem 2.24). The weak version (3-restricted valuations) is equivalent to ACA0 (Theorem 2.26).

statement.notation: VEL, Geach and GL frame definability on image-finite frames
statement.name: Image-finite versions
statement.definition: VEL and the frame-definability principles for Geach axioms and GL, restricted to image-finite frames.
statement.facts: All are equivalent to ACA0 over RCA0. The finite-frame versions are provable in RCA0 (Corollary 2.28).

statement.notation: VEL for modal predicate logic; frame definability for BF and CBF
statement.name: Predicate modal logic VEL and Barcan formulas
statement.definition: VEL for variable-domain Kripke frames (W,R,D), and frame definability for the Barcan formula (domain-decreasing frames) and the Converse Barcan formula (domain-increasing frames).
statement.facts: Each is equivalent to ACA+_0 over RCA0, as is the existence of a valuation on every predicate frame (Theorem 2.34).

statement.notation: VEL for CTL, Restricted VEL for CTL, VEL for image-finite CTL
statement.name: Valuation Extension Lemma for CTL
statement.definition: VEL for CTL valuations on serial frames. The restricted version uses n-restricted valuations. The image-finite version is restricted to image-finite serial frames.
statement.facts: Restricted VEL for CTL implies Π^1_1-CA0 over RCA0 (Theorem 3.9) and is provable in Π^1_1-CA0 + Σ^1_2-induction (Theorem 3.10). VEL for CTL is provable in Σ^1_2-DC0 (Corollary 3.11). VEL for image-finite CTL is equivalent to ACA+_0 over RCA0 (Theorem 3.15). Some CTL-valuation exists on every serial frame, provably in RCA0 (Theorem 3.16).

statement.name: Valuation Extension Lemma for LTL
statement.definition: For every LTL-frame (a single infinite path) and assignment v, there is an LTL-valuation extending v.
statement.facts: Implies ACA0 over RCA0 (Corollary 3.19) and is provable in ACA'_0 (Theorem 3.32). The restricted version is provable in ACA'_0 (Proposition 3.20). The exact strength is open (Questions 4.1 and 4.2).

items.quote: Over the latter, CΣ02 follows from but does not imply IPP (see Section 3.1 of [7]).
items.concerns: IPP matched to rt1inf.
reasons: attributed by the paper to Conidis–Slaman [7, Section 3.1]: cite the original

items.quote: Π01 G (but not IPP) is rΠ12 -conservative over RCA0
items.concerns: The parenthetical '(but not IPP)' is the only support, and it is cited. IPP is matched to rt1inf.
reasons: attributed by the paper to Hirschfeldt–Shore–Slaman [20]: cite the original

statement.name: Strong cohesive principle
statement.definition: COH together with IPP; equivalently cohesiveness with finitely many exceptions uniformly bounded. This is not the catalogue's stcoh (COH restricted to stable sequences).
statement.facts: Equivalent to StCADS over RCA0 (Proposition 5.9, from Hirschfeldt–Shore). Π^0_3-conservative over RCA0, citing [19]. Strictly weaker than ADS [19]. RT^2_2 and StCOH, even together with WKL, are Π^0_4-conservative over RCA0+IPP. Equivalent over RCA0 to Heine–Borel (Thm 5.15), Bolzano–Weierstrass (Thm 7.9), Arzelà–Ascoli (Thm 7.18), and to boundedness, uniform continuity and attainment of extrema for continuous functions on [0,1] (Thm 6.1), and to every bounded sequence of rationals having a Cauchy subsequence (Lemma 5.13, Kreuzer).

statement.notation: IVT, connectedness of R, finite sets of reals bounded, finite intersections of open sets open (slow Cauchy versions)
statement.name: First cluster of analytic principles for slow Cauchy reals
statement.definition: Intermediate value theorem, connectedness of R, boundedness of finite sets of reals, and openness of finite intersections of open sets, with reals as slow Cauchy sequences and continuous functions and open sets coded as in Definitions 3.1 and 4.1. This differs from the catalogue's ivt, which is the classical formulation.
statement.facts: Each is equivalent to IPP over RCA0 (IPP is catalogue rt1inf). IVT for strictly increasing functions and 'every continuous f : R → {0,1} is constant' are also equivalent to IPP.

statement.notation: HB, UC, Bounded, Extrema, Riemann, Weierstrass, BW, AA (slow Cauchy versions)
statement.name: Second cluster of analytic principles for slow Cauchy reals
statement.definition: Heine–Borel for [0,1], uniform continuity, boundedness and attainment of extrema of continuous f : [0,1] → R, Riemann integrability, the Weierstrass approximation theorem, Bolzano–Weierstrass and Arzelà–Ascoli, all in the slow-Cauchy representation. They differ from the catalogue's classical versions (heine-borel, ucont, cont-bounded, riemann, weierstrass, bwt).
statement.facts: Each is equivalent over RCA0 to StCOH. Riemann integrability and Weierstrass approximation are equivalent to COH over RCA0+IPP. The sequential Heine–Borel theorem is equivalent to ACA0 (Prop. 5.16).

statement.name: Baire category theorem (slow Cauchy reals)
statement.definition: The intersection of a family of dense open subsets of R is dense.
statement.facts: Provable in RCA0+IΣ^0_2 and also in RCA0+Π^0_1G. rΠ^1_2-conservative over RCA0, so it implies neither Σ^0_2-induction nor IPP. It does not imply Π^0_1G over RCA0. It implies that R is uncountable.

statement.name: R is uncountable
statement.definition: For every family of reals there is a real different from all of them.
statement.facts: Provable in RCA0+IPP. RCA0+WKL+uncountability is Π^1_1-conservative over RCA0, hence strictly weaker than IPP; RCA0+WKL+uncountability does not prove CΣ^0_2. It is open whether RCA0 proves it.

statement.notation: No finite dense family of reals
statement.name: Dense sets of reals are infinite
statement.definition: No finite collection (x_n)_{n≤N} of reals is dense in the order of R.
statement.facts: Equivalent to CΣ^0_2 over RCA0.

statement.name: Tietze extension theorem (slow Cauchy version)
statement.definition: Every continuous f : C → [−1,1] on a closed C ⊆ R extends to a continuous h : R → [−1,1].
statement.facts: Provable in RCA0+IΣ^0_2; exact strength unknown.

statement.name: Limit superior principle
statement.definition: Every bounded sequence of reals has an ε-approximation to its limit superior.
statement.facts: Equivalent to Σ^0_2-induction over RCA0.

statement.name: Iterates of continuous functions
statement.definition: For continuous f : [0,1] → [0,1] and x, there is a sequence of reals (x_n) with x_0 = x and x_{n+1} = f(x_n).
statement.facts: Equivalent to arithmetical comprehension over RCA0. For strong contractions it is provable in RCA0+StCOH (Banach fixed point theorem).

statement.name: Caristi's fixed point theorem (version)
statement.definition: For continuous f and lower semicontinuous g represented via Cauchy sequences, if g(f(x)) ≤ g(x) − |x − f(x)| for all x then f has a fixed point.
statement.facts: Provable in RCA0.

statement.name: Co-finite choice and its boundedness version
statement.definition: C_F is choice on non-empty co-finite subsets of N. B_F maps a left-c.e. real x to any upper bound in [x,∞).
statement.facts: B_F ≡sW C_F ≡W C_N (Proposition 3.3). C_N ≡W B_F is idempotent and is reduced to by LPO.

statement.name: Interval choice, proper interval choice and boundedness versions
statement.definition: Choice on non-empty closed intervals of [0,1] (C_I), on proper closed intervals (C_I^-), and the boundedness versions with sup q_n ≤ x ≤ inf r_n. B_I^+ allows r_n = ∞.
statement.facts: B_I ≡sW C_I and B_I^- ≡sW C_I^- (Proposition 3.6). IVT ≡sW C_I (Theorem 6.2). The chain LLPO < C_I^- < C_I < C_K ≡ WKL is strict, C_I^- < C_N, and C_N | C_I. C_I^- ≤W C_N, and C_I is not reducible to C_I^-.

statement.name: Compact choice
statement.definition: Choice on non-empty compact subsets of a computable metric space.
statement.facts: C_K(X) ≤sW LLPO^, with equality when {0,1}^N embeds computably into X (Theorem 2.10). C_K ≡W WKL, and HBT ≡W C_K (Theorem 7.1).

statement.name: Countable closed choice (the map A ↦ characteristic function of A)
statement.definition: The map taking a negative-information name of A ⊆ N to its characteristic function.
statement.facts: B ≡W C ≡W LPO^ (Proposition 3.7). C_A <W C (Proposition 4.8).

statement.name: Baire Category, Banach Inverse Mapping, Open Mapping, Closed Graph and Uniform Boundedness theorems as multi-valued operations
statement.definition: The realizers of these classical theorems on computable complete metric spaces and Banach spaces.
statement.facts: BCT_X ≡W C_N for any non-empty complete computable metric space X, and UBT_{X,Y} ≡W C_N for Banach spaces different from {0}. IMT, OMT and CGT are ≤W C_N, with equivalence on ℓ2.

statement.name: Brouwer Fixed Point Theorem and Weierstraß Approximation Theorem as operations
statement.definition: The realizers of BFT and WAT as multi-valued operations.
statement.facts: BFT ≤W WKL (Corollary 8.7) and computable fixed points have low names (Corollary 8.8). WAT ≡W id (Corollary 8.4).

statement.name: Iterated jump AST
statement.facts: AST(0) ≡ AST. AST(n) → AST(m) for m<n over RCA0 (Prop 4.3). AST(m) is the weakest natural principle failing in every ω-model of low_m sets. AST(m) is Π¹₁-conservative over RCA0. DNR(m) → AST(m) over RCA0. AST(n) does not hold in every ω-model of WKL(m) for m<n (Thm 4.6). Over RCA0, WKL(m) + ¬IΣ⁰_{m+1} → AST(n) (Kolodziejczyk, personal communication).

statement.name: Iterated jump DNR
statement.definition: ∀X ∃Y Y^(m) is DNC over X^(m).
statement.facts: DNR(0) ≡ RWWKL, and DNR(1) ↔ Seq*(TS) over RCA0. WWKL(m) → DNR(m) and DNR(m) → AST(m) over RCA0. WWKL(m) ⇏ DNR(m) over ω-models (Thm 4.5). DNR(m) is not implied over ω-models by WKL(n) for m<n (Thm 4.7). Its first-order part is unknown.

statement.name: Iterated jump WWKL
statement.definition: ∀X ∃Y Y^(m) computes a 1-random over X^(m).
statement.facts: WWKL(0) ≡ WWKL. WKL(m) → WWKL(m) and WWKL(m) → DNR(m) over RCA0. WKL(m) is not implied by WWKL(m) over ω-models (Thm 4.4). RCA0* ⊢ WWKL(m) → BΣ⁰_{m+1} (Kolodziejczyk, using FCKWY24).

statement.name: Iterated jump WKL
statement.definition: ∀X ∃Y Y^(m) ≫ X^(m) (Y^(m) is of PA degree over X^(m)).
statement.facts: WKL(0) ≡ WKL, and WKL(1) ↔ COH over RCA0. ACA → WKL(m), and WKL(m) → WWKL(m) over RCA0. RCA0* ⊢ WKL(m) → BΣ⁰_{m+1}. WKL(m) is Π¹₁-conservative over RCA0* + BΣ⁰_{m+1}. The WKL(m) are logically independent over ω-models (Belanger). Thm 4.4: WKL(m) is not implied by WWKL(m) over ω-models. Thm 4.6: for m<n, AST(n) is not implied by WKL(m) over ω-models. Thm 4.7: for m<n, DNR(m) is not implied by WKL(n) over ω-models.

statement.name: Sequential thin set theorem for singletons with finite errors
statement.definition: For every sequence ⟨f_i⟩ of functions N→N there is an infinite H such that for each i some H_i =* H has f_i(H_i) ≠ N.
statement.facts: ω-models of Seq*(TS1) are those I where each X ∈ I has Y ∈ I with Y′ DNC over X′ (Thm 2.17, cited). Equivalent to DNR(1). COH → Seq*(TS1) and RRT22 → Seq*(TS1) over RCA0; Seq*(TS1) → AST over RCA0. Seq*(TS1) is not implied by WKL, FIP or OPT over ω-models, and COH is not implied by it. New result Prop 3.2: RCA0 ⊢ Seq*(TS1) → OPT, strengthening COH → OPT and RRT22 → OPT.

statement.notation: lim ∘ ... von Stein operators: (id : A(N) → V(N)), (id : V(N) → A(N)), (id : R< → R)
statement.name: Identity maps between spaces of closed/overt sets and between R< and R
statement.definition: Identity maps from the space of closed subsets of N to overt subsets of N, the reverse, and from lower reals to reals.
statement.facts: All are Weihrauch equivalent to lim (von Stein). More generally, for a space X with a computable embedding of N, id : A(X) → V(X) and id : V(X) → A(X) are equivalent to lim (Corollaries 17, 19, 22, 23). For [0,1] both are equivalent to lim (Corollary 23).

statement.name: Hausdorff dimension of closed subsets of [0,1] (resp. as upper real)
statement.definition: The map A ↦ dim_H(A) from closed subsets of [0,1] to R, and the variant dim_H^> with output type R>.
statement.facts: dim_H ≡W lim ⋆ lim and dim_H^> ≡W lim (Theorem 48). Corollary 53: there is a computable closed and computably overt set whose Hausdorff dimension is Turing-equivalent to ∅''.

statement.name: Maximal flow on the infinite binary tree
statement.definition: Given a non-negative edge assignment f on the full binary tree, find a flow g ≤ f with g(ε) maximal.
statement.facts: MaxFlow ≡W lim.

statement.name: Non-zero flow
statement.definition: Given an edge assignment f, find a flow g ≤ f with g(ε) > 0.
statement.facts: NonZeroFlow ≡W C_N × C_{0,1}^N (≡ C_N × WKL) (Theorem 39), which is ≡W C_R (Corollary 57).

statement.name: Construct a measure supported in a closed set
statement.definition: Given a non-empty closed A ⊆ X, find a non-zero measure µ with supp(µ) ⊆ A.
statement.facts: ConstructMeasure_X ≡W C_X for a computable Polish space X (Theorem 34). ConstructMeasure[0,1] <W supp^{-1} (Corollary 35). ConstructMeasure[0,1] ≡W C[0,1] ≡W H1 C[0,1] (Figure 1).

statement.name: Support of a measure and inverse
statement.definition: supp maps a measure to its support (as overt set, or as closed set); supp^{-1} constructs a measure with a given closed set as support.
statement.facts: supp : M(X) → V(X) is computable. For X perfect (or with a computable embedding of N) and effectively locally compact, supp^A_X ≡W (supp^A_X)^{-1} ≡W lim (relative to the Halting problem otherwise).

statement.name: Frostman measure constructions
statement.definition: Given a closed A ⊆ [0,1] and s, find an s-Frostman measure supported in A (resp. with support exactly A).
statement.facts: Frost ≡W C_N × C[0,1] ≡W NonZeroFlow (Corollary 57); StrictFrost ≡W lim ≡W MaxFlow (Corollary 58).

statement.name: Closed choice on sets of positive Hausdorff dimension (resp. dimension 1)
statement.definition: Restriction of C[0,1] to closed sets of positive Hausdorff dimension, resp. dimension 1.
statement.facts: HC[0,1] ≡W H1 C[0,1] ≡W C[0,1] (via Shmerkin's construction).

statement.name: Perfect core and concentrated-measure operations
statement.definition: PerfectCore maps a closed set A to a closed and overt B ⊇ A with the same perfect kernel; Concentrate produces a concentrated non-atomic measure below a given one; ConcentratedSupport computes the support of a concentrated measure as closed and overt.
statement.facts: All three are computable.

statement.name: Upper bound for monotone bounded sequence of naturals
statement.definition: Given a monotone bounded sequence of naturals, find an upper bound.
statement.facts: Used to show WKL × UpperBound ≤W NonZeroFlow.

items.quote: Conidis and Slaman [21] showed that RRT22 is Π11 -conservative
items.citedFrom: Conidis and Slaman [21]; independently Wei Wang (unpublished)
reasons: attributed by the paper to Conidis and Slaman [21]; independently Wei Wang (unpublished): cite the original

statement.name: Bounded monotone enumeration
statement.loc: Section 4.3, outline of proof of Theorem 4.14
statement.definition: A principle capturing a 'k-dimensional exit tree' for Σ^0_1 sentences with k set constants G_0,...,G_{k-1}; it is preserved at each stage so that the iteration building a model of SRT^2_2 with only low sets can continue.
statement.facts: Its preservation is the key ingredient for iterating the construction in Theorem 4.14. The authors conjecture that the answer to Question 4.20 (is SRT^2_2 or RT^2_2 Π^1_1-conservative over RCA0 + BΣ^0_2) is negative and may be hidden within BME.

statement.name: (Induced) subgraph decision problems
statement.definition: For a computable graph G, IS_G(H)=1 iff G is isomorphic to an induced subgraph of H, and S_G(H)=1 iff G is isomorphic to a subgraph of H. The e-versions take graphs given by enumerations as input.
statement.facts: For finite G, LPO ≡sW S_G ≡sW IS_G, and for G not a complete graph LPO' ≡sW eIS_G (Theorem 3.17). For infinite c.e. G with R ⊑s G, or with K_ω not induced in G, the problems are ≡sW WF (Lemmas 3.18, 3.19), so there is no c.e. G with LPO <W IS_G <W WF (Theorem 3.20). For the trees T_{2k+1} and forests F_{2k+2}, S_G is ≡sW LPO^(2k) resp. LPO^(2k+1) (parallelized), by Theorem 3.22.

statement.name: (Induced) subgraph search problems
statement.definition: Given a graph H containing G as a (induced) subgraph, output a (induced) subgraph of H isomorphic to G. There are four variants (χχ, χe, eχ, ee) according to whether input and output graphs are given by characteristic function or by enumeration.
statement.facts: These problems are cylinders (Prop. 4.2) and are bounded above by C_NN (Prop. 4.3). IS-Copy_G ≡W C_NN, possibly relative to an oracle (Thm 4.5). S-Copy_G ≡W C_NN when G has only finitely many vertices of finite degree (Thm 4.6) and for G ∈ {L, C_n ⊔ R, K_m ⊔ R, 2^{<N}} (Prop. 4.14). S-Copy_G is computable for finite G (Thm 4.4) and for certain disjoint unions of finite graphs (Thm 4.39). IS-Copy of the disjoint union of all C_i (i≥3) is ≡W C_NN (Thm 4.40). S-Copy_R <W C_NN, and C_NN ≡W lim^2 ⋆ S-Copy_R (Cor. 4.16). S-Copy_R is incomparable with lim in some variants (Thm 4.18). The first-order part of S-Copy_R is that of C_NN (Prop. 4.17). S-Copy_{F_{2k+2}} ≤W the parallelization of LPO^(2k-1) (Thm 4.44).

statement.name: Ray embedding problem
statement.definition: Given a graph H isomorphic to G, where R ⊑s G, find a sequence p such that (p(i), p(i+1)) is an edge of H for every i.
statement.facts: These problems are cylinders (Prop. 4.11) and are ≤W C_NN (Lemma 4.12). R-Emb_R ≡W eR-Emb_R ≡W lim^2 (Prop. 4.15). R-Emb_G ⋆ S-Copy_R ≡W C_NN (Prop. 4.13).

statement.name: (k-)finitary part of a problem
statement.definition: Fin_k(f) is the most complex problem with codomain k that is Weihrauch reducible to f. Fin(f) is the countable coproduct of the Fin_k(f).
statement.facts: Fin(f) ≤W the first-order part of f. Fin(C_N) <W C_N ≡W the first-order part of C_N (Prop. 2.13). Fin(Con-S-Copy_R^{ee}) is computable (Thm 4.24).

statement.name: Lévy–Montague reflection scheme (Σ¹ₙ-Rfn)
statement.definition: For each L2 formula φ, every tuple of set parameters lies in a coded ω-model Y such that φ is absolute, at all parameters from Y, between Y and the universe. Σ¹ₙ-Rfn restricts the scheme to Σ¹ₙ and Π¹ₙ formulas, and Rfn is the union over n.
statement.facts: Rfn implies collection for all L2 formulas (Prop. 2.3). Over ACA0, Σ¹ₙ-Rfn is equivalent to strong Σ¹ₙ-DC (Thm 3.1). It is provable in WKL*0+¬IΣ01 (Thm 4.1). WKL0+Rfn is Π¹₁-conservative over RCA0 (Thm 5.20, Theorem A) and so over WKL0. Its first-order part is exactly IΣ1, and it is Π⁰₂-conservative over PRA (Cor. 5.21). WKL*0+Rfn is Π¹₁-conservative over RCA*0 (Cor. 5.22). The conservation does not extend to Σ¹₁ (Thm 6.1, Cor. 6.2), and Rfn is unprovable over RCA0 and WKL0. The conservation is proved in PRA+1-Con(Z2) (Thm 7.1).

statement.name: Strong Σ¹ₙ dependent choice
statement.definition: For η in Σ¹ₙ: ∃Z ∀n (∃Y η(n,(Z)<n,Y) → η(n,(Z)<n,(Z)n)).
statement.facts: Equivalent to Σ¹ₙ-Rfn over ACA0 (Thm 3.1).

items.quote: that RT2 is Π11 -conservative over BΣ03
items.concerns: Matched RT^2 with arbitrary number of colors to rt2. The base theory is RCA0 + BΣ^0_3.
reasons: attributed by the paper to Slaman and Yokoyama [1]: cite the original

statement.name: Ramsey-type principle for fallow colorings (finitely many colors)
statement.definition: Whenever c:[M]^2→[0,a] is a fallow coloring (c(x,z)∈{c(x,y),c(y,z)} for x<y<z), there is an infinite set S on which c is constant.
statement.facts: fRT<∞ + RCA0 implies BΣ^0_3 (Theorem 1.5), already for the stable version fSRT<∞ (Theorem 2.3). trRT<∞ implies fRT<∞. ADS implies fRT^n for all finite n.

statement.name: Fallow Erdős–Moser principle for finitely many colors
statement.definition: Whenever c:[M]^2→[0,a] is a finite coloring, there is an infinite S⊆M such that c restricted to [S]^2 is fallow.
statement.facts: Equivalent to EM× (Lemma 1.4). fEM<∞ + IΣ^0_2 is Π^1_1-conservative over IΣ^0_2 (Theorem 1.6, via Theorem 3.21 for the stable version fSEM<∞). WKL0 + fEM<∞ is Π̃^0_3-conservative over RCA0 (Theorems 1.7 and 4.6), hence does not imply IΣ^0_2 (Corollary 4.7). fEM<∞ implies EM<∞.

statement.name: Erdős–Moser principle for finitely many colors
statement.definition: Whenever c:[M]^2→[0,a] is a finite coloring, there is an infinite S⊆M such that c restricted to [S]^2 is transitive (c(x,y)=c(y,z) implies c(x,z)=c(x,y)).
statement.facts: EM<∞ + IΣ^0_2 is Π^1_1-conservative over IΣ^0_2. It may be strictly weaker than fEM<∞, and it is not clear that it solves finitely many simultaneous EM instances.

statement.name: Ramsey-type principle for transitive colorings (finitely many colors)
statement.definition: Whenever c:[M]^2→[0,a] is a transitive coloring, there is an infinite S such that c restricted to [S]^2 is constant.
statement.facts: trRT^2 is equivalent to ADS. trRT<∞ + RCA0 implies BΣ^0_3, because it implies fRT<∞. It is unknown whether trRT^n implies trRT^{n+1}.

statement.name: Simultaneous Erdős–Moser principle
statement.definition: For every finite collection of colorings c_i:[M]^2→{0,1} there is an infinite S on which every c_i is transitive.
statement.facts: Equivalent to fEM<∞ (Lemma 1.4).

statement.name: Erdős–Moser principle for infinitely many colors
statement.definition: For every coloring c:[M]^2→M there is an infinite S such that c restricted to [S]^2 is transitive.
statement.facts: ACA0 implies EM∞ (Lemma 5.4). It is open whether EM∞ implies ACA0 (Question 5.5).

statement.name: Stable versions of fRT<∞ and fEM<∞
statement.definition: The versions of fRT<∞ and fEM<∞ restricted to stable colorings (for every x, c(x,n) is eventually constant).
statement.facts: fSRT<∞ + RCA0 implies BΣ^0_3 (Theorem 2.3). fSEM<∞ is Π^1_1-conservative over RCA0 + IΣ^0_2 (Theorem 3.21).

statement.name: Second-order primitive recursive arithmetic
statement.definition: PRA with function variables and defining equations for all primitive recursive functionals. It is function-based, and its minimal omega-model consists of the primitive recursive functions. It is the base theory of the paper.
statement.facts: PRA2 proves Δ⁰₀ induction, comprehension and bounded choice. It does not prove IΣ⁰₁, IΔ⁰₁ or Δ⁰₁-CA. It is arithmetically conservative over PRA. RCA0 is identified with PRA2 + QF-AC. The paper compares PRA2 with RCA0* (Remark 2.30), whose minimal model contains non-primitive-recursive recursive functions.

statement.name: Quantifier-free axiom of choice (function-based RCA0)
statement.definition: Schema: ∀n∃m θ(n,m) → ∃f ∀n θ(n,f(n)) for quantifier-free θ.
statement.facts: Over PRA2, QF-AC implies Δ⁰₁-CA and IΣ⁰₁, and is equivalent to totality of minimisation (Proposition 2.22). It is identified with RCA0.

statement.name: Set-based recursive comprehension over PRA2
statement.definition: Comprehension for Σ⁰₁/Π⁰₁-equivalent formulas giving {0,1}-valued functions; 2^N-RCA0 = IΣ⁰₁ ∧ Δ⁰₁-CA.
statement.facts: Δ⁰₁-CA and IΣ⁰₁ are incomparable over PRA2. Both are strictly weaker than RCA0 over PRA2. Δ⁰₁-CA ∧ IΣ⁰₁ does not imply RCA0. WKL0 is strictly stronger than Δ⁰₁-CA over PRA2. RT^n_k (n,k>=2) is incomparable with Δ⁰₁-CA over PRA2.

statement.name: Baire category theorem for N^N
statement.definition: Given a sequence of dense open subsets of N^N, find a function in their intersection.
statement.facts: Over PRA2, it lies strictly between PRA2 and RCA0 (Theorem 4.2). It neither implies nor is implied by Δ⁰₁-CA or 2^N-RCA0 (Theorem 4.6). It is cited that over RCA0* it implies IΣ⁰₁ [Sim14].

statement.notation: Categoricity of DLO, random graph, atomless Boolean algebras
statement.name: Countable categoricity principles
statement.definition: Any two countable dense linear orders without endpoints (resp. random graphs, atomless Boolean algebras) are isomorphic, with the inverse isomorphism also existing.
statement.facts: Each is equivalent to RCA0 over PRA2.

statement.notation: IntermediateValueTheorem, Completeness of R, HeineBorelTheorem (problem forms)
statement.name: Problem forms of analysis theorems
statement.definition: Instances are presentations of functions, Cauchy sequences, or covers of [0,1] by rational open intervals. Solutions are a point where the function is discontinuous or zero, the limit, or an uncovered point.
statement.facts: Over PRA2, HeineBorelTheorem is equivalent to WKL0 (Proposition 6.5). IntermediateValueTheorem is conjectured to be equivalent to Δ⁰₁-CA over PRA2 (Proposition 5.8). For each of these, every computable instance has a primitive recursive instance whose solutions compute a solution (Theorem 5.4).

statement.name: Baer type problem
statement.definition: Given a Baer categorical rank 1 torsion-free abelian group, output its Baer type, i.e. the set {m : m | g} for a nonzero g.
statement.facts: Every c.e. degree is the degree of the solutions of some computable instance. The only primitive recursive instance is the trivial group (Proposition 5.11).

statement.notation: Szpilrajn, graph reorientation, Rival–Sands for honest graphs, Hall's theorem variants, connected components
statement.name: Combinatorial principles done in PRA2
statement.definition: Szpilrajn's theorem; transitive reorientation of pseudo-transitive oriented graphs; Rival–Sands and (2n-1)-colouring for honestly presented locally finite graphs; Hall's theorem for finite A or under the extended Hall condition; existence of connected components.
statement.facts: The first four are proved in PRA2 (Propositions 3.11–3.13). Existence of connected components, under the hypothesis that finitely many vertices have every vertex connected to one of them, is equivalent to 2^N-RCA0 over PRA2 (Proposition 3.14).

statement.name: Domination principle
statement.definition: Every weakly represented family F of functions has a function g that dominates it, i.e. g(x) > f(x) for all sufficiently large x, for every f in F.
statement.facts: Equivalent over RCA0 to HIGH (Proposition 5, formalised Martin's theorem). RCA0 + DOM + BΣ02 proves IΣ0n for all n, hence PA (Theorem 6, from Hölzl–Raghavan–Stephan–Zhang). RCA0 + DOM is Π11-conservative over RCA0, so DOM does not imply BΣ02 (Theorem 8). Over RCA0 + IΣ02, DOM ↔ ¬MAD (Theorem 14); over RCA0 + BΣ02 the same holds (Corollary 16). DOM → AVOID, DOM → HI (Proposition 24), and (DOM ∨ DNR) ↔ AVOID over RCA0 (Proposition 20, Kjos-Hanssen–Merkle–Stephan). In ω-models DOM fails for the ω-model of sets of low-for-ML-random degree (Example 25), so HI does not imply DOM.

statement.name: Maximal almost disjoint family principle
statement.definition: There is a non-finite, weakly represented family of infinite sets that is maximal almost disjoint.
statement.facts: Over RCA0 + IΣ02, DOM ↔ ¬MAD (Theorem 14); also over RCA0 + BΣ02 (Corollary 16). RCA0 + BΣ02 + ¬IΣ02 proves MAD (Proposition 15). MAD is equivalent to ¬DOM in ω-models (Hölzl–Raghavan–Stephan–Zhang).

statement.name: Maximal eventually different family principle
statement.definition: There is a weakly represented family F of functions such that any two functions in F are equal or eventually different, and every function coincides infinitely often with some function in F.
statement.facts: RCA0 ⊢ MED → ¬AVOID (Theorem 19). Every topped model of RCA0 + BΣ02 + ¬IΣ02 satisfies MED (Proposition 22). The situation without BΣ02 is left as an open question.

statement.name: Avoidance principle
statement.definition: For every weakly represented family F of functions there is a function g that is eventually different from all f in F.
statement.facts: RCA0 ⊢ (DOM ∨ DNR) ↔ AVOID (Proposition 20, Kjos-Hanssen–Merkle–Stephan). MED → ¬AVOID over RCA0 (Theorem 19).

statement.name: Hyperimmunity principle
statement.definition: For every weakly represented family F of functions there is a function g such that for every f in F, g(x) > f(x) for unboundedly many x.
statement.facts: RCA0 ⊢ DOM → HI (Proposition 24). HI does not imply DOM (Example 25). RCA0 + IΣ02 + HI is Π11-conservative over RCA0 + IΣ02 (Theorem 26). RCA0 + HI ⊢ BI (Proposition 28).

statement.name: Bi-immunity principle
statement.definition: For every weakly represented family F of infinite sets there is a set B such that no A in F is a subset of B or of its complement.
statement.facts: RCA0 + HI ⊢ BI (Proposition 28). BI is Π11-conservative over RCA0 (Theorem 29), so BI does not imply HI.

statement.name: Determinacy of finite differences of open sets on Cantor space
statement.definition: For every n, every Gale–Stewart game on {0,1} whose payoff is a (possibly nonstandard) n-fold difference of Σ⁰₁ sets is determined.
statement.facts: Over ACA0 it is equivalent to ACA'0 (Propositions 3, 4) and to Π¹₂-Ref(ACA0) (Theorem 15); in particular it is equivalent to a Π¹₂ sentence.

statement.name: Determinacy of finite differences of open sets on Baire space
statement.definition: For every n, every Gale–Stewart game on N whose payoff is an n-fold difference of Σ⁰₁ sets is determined.
statement.facts: Over ACA0 it is equivalent to Π¹₁-CA'0 and to Π¹₃-Ref(Π¹₁-CA0) (Theorem 12).

statement.name: Determinacy of finite differences of Σ⁰₂ sets
statement.definition: For every n, every Gale–Stewart game on N whose payoff is an n-fold difference of Σ⁰₂ sets is determined.
statement.facts: Over ACA0 it is equivalent to Π¹₃-Ref(Π¹₂-CA0) and to ∀n.[Σ¹₁]n-ID (Theorem 16). Over RCA0 it is equivalent to its Cantor-space version ∀n.(Σ⁰₂)n-Det* (Proposition 5).

statement.name: Determinacy of finite differences of Σ⁰₃ sets
statement.definition: For every n, every Gale–Stewart game on N whose payoff is an n-fold difference of Σ⁰₃ sets is determined.
statement.facts: Over ACA0 it is equivalent to Π¹₃-Ref(Z2) (Theorem 29). This uses Montalbán–Shore: Π¹ₘ₊₂-CA0 proves (Π⁰₃)m-Det, and (Π⁰₃)m-Det proves the existence of β-models of Δ¹ₘ-CA0.

statement.name: Π¹₁-CA0 with finite iterated hyperjumps
statement.definition: RCA0 plus: for all n and X there is a chain of coded β-models X ∈ X0 ∈ ... ∈ Xn with each model a β-submodel of the next (equivalently, HJ^n(X) exists).
statement.facts: Equivalent over ACA0 to ∀n.(Σ⁰₁)n-Det and to Π¹₃-Ref(Π¹₁-CA0) (Theorem 12).

statement.name: Reflection principle for Π¹ₙ sentences over T
statement.definition: ∀φ ∈ Π¹ₙ. Pr_T(⌜φ⌝) → Tr_{Π¹ₙ}(⌜φ⌝), for a finitely axiomatizable theory T extending ACA0.
statement.facts: Equivalent to the uniform reflection scheme Π¹ₙ-RFN(T) over ACA0 (Proposition 2). Characterized by chains of coded models (Theorem 8). Characterizes the determinacy principles ∀n.(Σ⁰ₖ)n-Det(*) via Π¹₂-Ref(ACA0), Π¹₃-Ref(Π¹₁-CA0), Π¹₃-Ref(Π¹₂-CA0), Π¹₃-Ref(Z2).

statement.name: Iterated Σ¹₁ inductive definitions
statement.definition: The existence of sets inductively defined by combinations of k Σ¹₁ transfinite-induction operators.
statement.facts: Over ATR0, MedSalem–Tanaka show (Σ⁰₂)k-Det ↔ [Σ¹₁]k-ID. In this paper ∀n.(Σ⁰₂)n-Det implies ∀n.[Σ¹₁]n-ID over ATR0 (Proposition 7), and ∀n.[Σ¹₁]n-ID implies ∀n.ψ₁(2,n) over ACA0 (Lemma 18).

statement.name: Strong Σ¹ₖ dependent choice
statement.definition: ACA0 plus a scheme asserting ∃Z∀n∀Y.(η(n,(Z)_n,Y) → η(n,(Z)_n,(Z)^n)) for Σ¹ₖ formulas η.
statement.facts: Equivalent over ACA0 to Π¹ₖ-CA0 for k = 1, 2 (Simpson VII.6.9), and to the existence for every X of a βk-model containing X.

statement.name: Rival–Sands theorem for k-chain decomposable partial orders
statement.definition: Every infinite partial order that comes with a decomposition into k chains has a (0,∞)-homogeneous chain. RSpo^CD_<∞ is ∀k RSpo^CD_k.
statement.facts: RSpo^CD_3 → ADS (Lemma 6.1). RSpo^CD_2 ↔ SADS over RCA0 (Theorem 6.6(3)). RSpo^CD_<∞ → IΣ02 (Lemma 6.3). RSpo^CD_<∞ ↔ RSpo_<∞ ↔ IΣ02 + ADS over RCA0. RSpo_k ↔ RSpo^CD_k for k ≥ 3 over RCA0 (Theorem 6.6(2)). RSpo_2 ↔ RSpo^CD_2 over WKL0.

statement.name: Rival–Sands theorem with 'cofinitely many'
statement.definition: Every infinite partial order of width ≤ k (resp. k-chain decomposable) has a (0,cof)-homogeneous chain, that is, every element is comparable with none or with cofinitely many elements of the chain.
statement.facts: (0,cof)-RSpo_2, (0,cof)-RSpo^CD_2 and ADS are pairwise equivalent over RCA0 + IΣ02 (Theorem 6.6(5)). Π^1_1-CA0 proves (0,cof)-RSpo_<∞ (Theorem 4.10). (0,cof)-RSpo^CD_2 → ADS (Lemma 6.4). The exact strength of (0,cof)-RSpo_<∞ is open (Question 6.7).

statement.name: Infinite chain for partial orders of bounded width; infinite antichain for partial orders of bounded height
statement.definition: CC_k: every infinite partial order of width ≤ k has an infinite chain. CA_k: every infinite partial order of height ≤ k has an infinite antichain.
statement.facts: RCA0 proves CC_k and CA_k for each fixed standard k (Proposition 3.8). CC_<∞, CA_<∞ and BΣ02 are pairwise equivalent over RCA0.

statement.name: n-stable Ramsey's theorem for pairs
statement.definition: RT^2_k restricted to k-colorings of pairs such that for every x at most n values y > x have c(x,y) ≠ c(x,y+1).
statement.facts: RCA0 proves n-stable SRT^2_k for fixed standard n and k. For fixed n, BΣ02 ↔ n-stable SRT^2_<∞ over RCA0, and IΣ02 ↔ ∀n (n-stable SRT^2_<∞) over RCA0 (Proposition 5.8).

statement.notation: Rival–Sands for partial orders without infinite antichains
statement.name: Extension of Rival–Sands to partial orders with no infinite antichain
statement.definition: Every infinite partial order with no infinite antichain has a (0,∞)- (resp. (0,cof)-) homogeneous chain.
statement.facts: The (0,∞) version is equivalent to ACA0 over RCA0, and equivalent to the version for well-partial-orders (Theorem 7.8). Π^1_1-CA0 proves the (0,cof) version (Theorem 7.2). The exact strength of the (0,cof) version is open (Question 7.9).
